texts: In truncus arteriosus the left coronary artery typically originates from the left portion of the truncal root: B.
The right coronary artery usually arises from the right anterior part; a single coronary artery occurs in a minority, roughly 5 to 20 percent, and two ostia are the rule.
Abnormal origins, a high or slit-like ostium and intramural courses matter when the pulmonary arteries are detached from the trunk.
In the picture, the root of the crown's left spike leaves the left side of the tree trunk.
Memory hook: the left spike grows from the left of the trunk.
